text.p: These are the main stories in Latvian newspapers on Monday. Prepared for Reuters by the Co-operation Fund. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- The minister of defence, Talavs Jundzis, told a news conference on Friday that Latvia's defense forces are suffering from a shortage of funds.
- Finance Minister Roberts Zile said on Friday that the new government's fiscal and economic policies will not differ greatly from those of the previous administration.
- An international conference entitled "Women and Men in dialogue" has closed its sessions in Valmiera. It was attended by nearly 1,500 participants from 11 countries.

- Latvia and Egypt are expected to sign several agreements when an intergovernmental committee meets in Riga from August 11-13. Among them are agreements on tourism, shipping, culture, health, and suspension of visa requirements for diplomats.

- A new passenger/cargo ferry line is to be opened today between Ventspils and the German port of Kiel by Latvia's Seastar and Germany's Zerssen-Baltic. It will be serviced by a Ro Ro-type ferry boat which will make two trips per week.
